introduction-the-dependency-nightmare.core: Once state is split into many stacks, orchestration becomes the problem: copy-pasted backend and provider blocks in every directory, outputs that must be passed between stacks, and an apply order someone has to remember. Orchestrators such as Terragrunt, Spacelift and Terraform Cloud/HCP Stacks keep configuration DRY, model dependencies, and run stacks in the right order.

first_principles.problem: Bringing up a new region means manually applying 30 directories in an order documented on a stale wiki page.
truths: Order should be computed, not remembered.

analogy.title: A project manager for construction crews
analogy.story: Instead of crews calling each other, a schedule says who goes after whom and hands over the measurements.
analogy.breaks: Crews adapt; orchestrators need explicit declarations.

example.title: Before orchestration
flow: Engineer copies VPC ID into tfvars

check.q: What three problems do stack orchestrators solve?
check.a: Repeated boilerplate configuration, dependency ordering, and passing outputs between stacks.

terragrunt-dependencies.core: Terragrunt wraps Terraform. A root terragrunt.hcl generates backend and provider blocks for every child using path-derived keys, include blocks inherit common config, and dependency blocks read another unit's outputs and add it to the run graph. `terragrunt run-all apply` (or `run --all`) applies everything in dependency order, in parallel where possible.

first_principles.problem: Each of 30 stacks has a slightly different, hand-written backend key, and two collide.

analogy.title: A family recipe book with a shared preface
analogy.story: Every recipe inherits the kitchen rules from the preface and lists which other recipes must be cooked first.
analogy.breaks: Recipes don't produce outputs; units pass real IDs.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: No backend boilerplate; VPC applied first automatically.

check.q: How does Terragrunt know to apply vpc before app?
check.a: The dependency block in app declares vpc, so it's placed earlier in the run graph.

mocking-for-the-first-run.core: On a brand-new environment, `run-all plan` fails because dependency outputs don't exist yet: the VPC hasn't been applied, so app can't read vpc_id. Terragrunt's mock_outputs supply placeholder values for plan and validate, restricted by mock_outputs_allowed_terraform_commands so real applies always use real outputs.

first_principles.problem: CI can't produce a plan for a new region because downstream stacks error on missing outputs.
truths: Plans need values for all inputs.
Upstream outputs don't exist before apply.

analogy.title: Placeholder text in a page layout
analogy.story: 'Lorem ipsum' lets you design the page before the real copy arrives; you'd never print it.
analogy.breaks: Readers spot lorem ipsum; Terraform would happily use a fake ID if allowed.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: New-region plan works; apply uses real outputs.

check.q: Why restrict mock_outputs to validate and plan?
check.a: So an apply never creates resources using fake IDs; it must wait for real upstream outputs.

saas-orchestration-spacelift-and-terrafo.core: Managed platforms (Spacelift, HCP Terraform/Terraform Cloud, env0, Scalr) run Terraform for you: remote runs with logs, state storage, policy checks (OPA or Sentinel), private module registries, drift detection, and stack dependencies that pass outputs and trigger downstream runs. You trade self-hosting effort and some flexibility for governance and less undifferentiated work.

first_principles.problem: A team spends a sprint a quarter maintaining Atlantis, runners, policy hooks and drift jobs.
truths: Running IaC pipelines is undifferentiated work.

analogy.title: A managed print service vs your own printers
analogy.story: You stop buying toner and fixing jams, and get usage reports and access control included.
analogy.breaks: Print jobs are simple; infra platforms need network access to private resources.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: VPC change triggers app run with new output.

check.q: Why would a SaaS IaC platform need private workers?
check.a: To reach private APIs and resources (and keep credentials) inside your network rather than from the vendor's runners.
